questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

Bindu asked Rekha if Komal was spying on her.
options_en: Bindu said to Rekha, "Komal is spying on you?"
Bindu said to Rekha, "Is Komal spying on you?"
Bindu said to Rekha, "Was Komal spying on you?"
Bindu said to Rekha, "Had Komal been spying on you?"
questions.solution_en:
In the case of sentences like this where the sentence takes an Interrogative form in Direct Speech, "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "asked", etc. in Indirect Speech is changed into "said" in Direct Speech.

In Direct speech, the verb is always placed before the subject, unlike in Indirect Speech. Thus, option (a) is incorrect.

If there is a question whose answer can come as "Yes" or "No", we should use "If" or "Whether" before the Indirect Speech and "Is/are/am/was/were" before the Direct Speech.

For example:

Sushma asked me if she was cooking. (Indirect Speech)

Sushma said to me, "Is she cooking?" (Direct Speech)

The tense of the Indirect Speech is in the Past Continuous Tense. So, the tense in the Direct Speech will be in the Present Continuous Tense.

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

Indirect SpeechDirect Speech
asked.. ifsaid to
Komal was spyingIs Komal spying
heryou

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.solution_en:
Option (c) is the correct choice.

RULE - If the given sentence in Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Continuous Tense, the same sentence in Direct Speech would be in either Present Perfect Continuous Tense or Past Continuous Tense or the same tense.

Past Perfect Continuous (Subject + had + been + V1-ing + Object) would be converted into Present Perfect Continuous (Subject + has/have + been + V1-ing + Object) or Past Continuous (Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object).

Here is the case of Past Perfect Continuous Tense to Present Perfect Continuous Tense.

For example:

He said that they had been waiting for hours. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "We have been waiting for hours". (Direct Speech)

Also, when changing the sentence from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech, usually used conjunction 'that', between the reporting verb and the speech, is removed.

The following changes will be made in the sentence when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

Indirect SpeechDirect Speech
ToldSaid to
SheI
Hadhave
The previouslast

Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank.

The ointment helped ___ the cut on her finger within a few days.
questions.solution_en:
The most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank is 'heal'. "Heal" means to become healthy again, especially after an injury or illness. The given sentence suggests that the ointment helped the cut on her finger recover within a few days. Other options do not fit the context of the sentence. "He'll" is a contraction of "he will". "Heel" refers to the back part of the foot below the ankle. "Hell" is a place regarded in various religions as a spiritual realm of evil and suffering.

The complete sentence is: The ointment helped heal the cut on her finger within a few days.

Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in future tense form.

There are many exciting activities planned for the festival.
options_en: There were many exciting activities planned for the festival.
There will be many exciting activities planned for the festival.
There have been many exciting activities planned for the festival.
There had been many exciting activities planned for the festival.
questions.solution_en: The option that expresses the given sentence in future tense form is (b) (There will be many exciting activities planned for the festival). This option suggests that there are plans to organize numerous exciting activities for the festival that is yet to come. Option (a) is in the past tense, indicating that the activities were planned in the past. Option (c) is in the present perfect tense, suggesting that the activities have been planned up to the present time. Option (d) is in the past perfect tense, indicating that the activities were planned before a specific past time. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.
